body:
FIXED. The masked-attention CPU kernel had an F32 arm guarded on the QUERY dtype alone and an F64 arm guarded on nothing. A mixed set — an F32 query against an F64 additive mask, which is what a trainable relative-position bias produces — matched the first guard and panicked reading the mask, or fell past it and panicked reading the query. The F32 arm now requires every tensor it reads to be F32, and the F64 fallthrough checks the same and hands anything mixed to the reference kernel, which reads through the dtype-agnostic accessor and is where this op went before the CPU kernel existed.

HOW IT REACHED MAIN: the only test exercising the shape trains a model and is skipped under -short, the lane CI runs. It had been panicking on the full suite. Found incidentally while benchmarking an unrelated llamagpu function whose test drives this path.

GATE: TestMHAMaskedMixedDtypeDoesNotPanic covers both mixings and asserts the result matches the reference kernel bit for bit, not merely that nothing panics. Restoring either the query-only guard or the missing delegation reddens it.

CHECK DRAFTED AND WITHHELD. PS3034 dtype-guard-misses-an-operand caught its motivating site exactly (4 findings pre-fix, 0 after) but reported 126 tree-wide, and the first sampled findings were all false. Two distinct noise sources, both diagnosed: (1) the dtype constraint is frequently SPLIT between an enclosing switch on one tensor dtype and an inner if on another, and a predicate reading only the if condition sees half the guard; (2) OUTPUT tensors are routinely allocated with the input dtype, so reading them as that dtype is guaranteed by construction rather than by the guard. A sound version needs to treat an enclosing type switch as part of the guard and to recognize outputs allocated from an input dtype. Recorded so a later attempt starts from the diagnosis.

RELATED: PS3027 is the same mistake on the OUTPUT side and did ship, because there the predicate is narrow — an INPUT view helper applied to a locally allocated output — with no equivalent noise.
